risk_review.notes: Reviewed the complete current Definition and its model-data and Wilsonian-action suppliers. The added Polish topology generating the Borel sigma-algebra specifies the topology required for low-field open patches and continuity; no topology-independent continuity is inferred. Absolute integrability of the product integral permits Fubini, giving Z_next=e^{c_j}Z_current; compatible logarithm branches are additional adopted data, not a consequence of nonvanishing alone. Nonzero partitions, local logarithms, admissible single-valued local sum, equivariance and all retained sectors are explicit hypotheses. Empty high-coordinate sets give the identity integral. No arbitrary continuum flow, continuum limit or empirical conclusion is asserted. Direct consumers are the matching theorem and counterterm example; their uses of the branchwise identity are compatible with this topology clarification.

citations.quote:
Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets. Fix their coefficient field $\mathbb K$ as part of the model and restrict its nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra, with $s^2=d_H^2=sd_H+d_Hs=0$. The model supplies two $\mathbb K$-linear subspaces

$$\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{0,4},\qquad\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,3}.$$

Here $\mathcal C$ is exactly the space of admissible changes of local background counterterm density, with coefficients and units giving dimensionless integrated action changes. The space $\mathcal N$ is exactly the space of boundary primitives whose $d_H$-derivatives are discarded in the infinitesimal variation under the stated support or boundary conditions. This convention must hold on every admitted background and ghost input; a surface contribution that is not discarded is not an element of $d_H\mathcal N$. Linearity of these two spaces is explicit model input, not a consequence of locality or nilpotence. No linear span of a restricted admissibility set is taken implicitly. If quantization or other restrictions instead make the admissible changes nonlinear, this vector-space quotient does not apply to them without a separately specified equivalence structure.

The space of compatible Wess–Zumino cocycles and the space of admissible changes are

$$Z^{1,4}:=\{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}:sa+d_Hb=0\text{ for some }b\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}\},\qquad B_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}:=s\mathcal C+d_H\mathcal N.$$

Both are linear spaces, and $B_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}\subseteq Z^{1,4}$: for $a=sc+d_Hn$ choose the ghost-number-two three-form $b=sn$, giving $sa+d_Hb=s^2c+sd_Hn+d_Hsn=0$. More generally, if $sa+d_Hb=0$, then $a'=a+sc+d_Hn$ obeys $sa'+d_H(b+sn)=0$, so every admitted representative change preserves consistency. The witness space for $b$ has bidegree $(2,3)$ and is distinct from the boundary-ambiguity space $\mathcal N$ of bidegree $(1,3)$.

An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a specified $a_4\in Z^{1,4}$ for the model's quantum background variation. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** is its class in

$$H^{1,4}_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}(s\mid d_H):=Z^{1,4}/B_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N},\qquad a'_4\sim a_4\ \Longleftrightarrow\ a'_4-a_4=sc+d_Hn\text{ for some }c\in\mathcal C,\ n\in\mathcal N.$$

The subspace property makes this an equivalence relation and a quotient vector space. Its class is zero exactly when $a_4=sc+d_Hn$ for some such $c,n$; adding the admissible counterterm density $-c$ then leaves only the discarded term $d_Hn$. Conversely, if adding an admissible density $c'$ leaves a discarded term, $a_4+sc'=d_Hn$, then $a_4=s(-c')+d_Hn$ has zero class. This is precisely cancellation of the infinitesimal local background variation in the declared convention. The ordinary unrestricted relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ is the special case $\mathcal C=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{0,4}$ and $\mathcal N=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,3}$ with a boundary convention discarding all these total derivatives; it is not substituted for a restricted model quotient.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

Assume Countable Choice: every countable family of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Fix an even integer $d\ge2$ and a compact smooth oriented Riemannian $d$-manifold $M$ without boundary. Use the negative-square real Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}_{0,d}$, generated by $\mathbb R^d$ with $vw+wv=-2\langle v,w\rangle$. The group $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$ is its subgroup generated by even products of unit vectors; its standard double cover acts by $v\mapsto svs^{-1}$ on $\mathbb R^d$ and has kernel $\{1,-1\}$. These are the Spin and covering conventions of the given-Spin-structure supplier. A smooth principal right $G$-bundle has a free, fiberwise transitive smooth right action and equivariant local trivializations by diffeomorphisms to $U\times G$; $G$ is a finite-dimensional real Lie group. A connection is a supplied smooth right-invariant horizontal complement $H$ to $\ker d\pi$ in the tangent bundle of its total space. Let $F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(M)$ be its principal right $\mathrm{SO}(d)$-bundle of positively oriented orthonormal frames. A specified spin structure is a principal right $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$-bundle $Q\to M$ with a smooth equivariant double-cover map $\lambda:Q\to F^+_{\mathrm{SO}}(M)$ covering the standard double covering $\rho:\operatorname{Spin}(d)\to\mathrm{SO}(d)$. The Levi-Civita connection lifts to a connection on $Q$. Fix an irreducible complex Clifford representation on a Hermitian space $\Delta$ of dimension $2^{d/2}$, with skew-Hermitian vector action $c_\Delta$. Put $\Gamma=i^{d/2}c_\Delta(e_1)\cdots c_\Delta(e_d)$ in a positively oriented orthonormal basis and $\Delta^\pm=\ker(\Gamma\mp I)$. The restrictions of the even Clifford action to these eigenspaces are the half-spin representations $\rho_\pm$ of $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$. Define $S^\pm=Q\times_{\rho_\pm}\Delta^\pm$. Let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $G$-bundle with connection $A$, let $V_R$ be a finite-dimensional Hermitian complex vector space, and let $R:G\to U(V_R)$ be a smooth group homomorphism. Set $E_R=P\times_R V_R=(P\times V_R)/G$ for the right action $(p,v)g=(pg,R(g)^{-1}v)$, so $[pg,v]=[p,R(g)v]$. The associated-bundle and covariant-derivative supplier supplies its smooth complex bundle charts (using the underlying real representation for the real associated-bundle definition). In a smooth local section $s$ of $P$, write $A_s=s^*\omega$, where $\omega$ is the principal connection form of $H$, and define the induced connection by $\nabla^A\psi=d\psi+(dR)_e(A_s)\psi$. The supplier proves that this formula patches with the stated quotient convention under Countable Choice. Since $R$ is unitary, the fiber metric $\langle[p,v],[p,w]\rangle=\langle v,w\rangle_{V_R}$ is well-defined and this connection preserves it. Let $c:TM\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(S^+\oplus S^-)$ be the skew-Hermitian Clifford action, with $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2g(v,w)$ for $v,w\in T_xM$, and let $\nabla$ be the tensor-product connection induced by the lifted Levi-Civita connection and $A$. The chiral Dirac operator is the extension to the stated Sobolev spaces of the first-order expression in any positively oriented local orthonormal frame $(e_i)$; this expression is independent of that frame.

$$D^+_{A,R}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E_R)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R),\qquad D^+_{A,R}\psi=\sum_{i=1}^{d} c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}\psi\quad(\psi\in C^\infty(M;S^+\otimes E_R)),$$

where $L^2$ is the completion for the bundle metric and Riemannian volume, and $H^1$ is the completion of smooth sections in the norm $\|\psi\|_{H^1}^2=\|\psi\|_2^2+\|\nabla\psi\|_2^2$. These are complex Hilbert spaces. The smooth first-order expression is bounded from $H^1$ to $L^2$. Assume it is Fredholm in the bounded Banach-space sense: its range is closed and its kernel and quotient cokernel $L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R)/\operatorname{ran}D^+_{A,R}$ are finite dimensional. Its index is their complex dimension difference. Its inverse determinant line is

$$\mathcal L_A=\left(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+_{A,R}\right)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+_{A,R},$$

Here $\det_{\mathbb C}W=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}W}_{\mathbb C}W$, including $\det0=\mathbb C$. Our phrase **inverse determinant line** means the dual of $\Delta_A=\det\ker D^+\otimes(\det\operatorname{coker}D^+)^*$; the displayed $\mathcal L$ is the line called $\mathrm{Det}$, not $\mathrm{Det}^{-1}$, in Dai–Freed §2. This explicit formula fixes the convention throughout.

The named regularized geometry means the following supplied **admissible analytic data**, rather than an arbitrary Hermitian line relabeled by a name. Test smooth dependence on each finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold $T$ of connections on the fixed $M,P,R$. Write $\mathscr H^\pm=T\times L^2(M;S^\pm\otimes E_R)$ with common first-Sobolev domains. Supply unitary parameter connections $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ on these Hilbert bundles, preserving smooth sections and the Sobolev domains; for the fixed product identification one may take the ordinary derivative in $T$. Fix a positive inverse-length scale $\mu$ and put $\mathscr D=D^+/\mu$, with Hilbert adjoint $\mathscr D^*$. These choices and the local-counterterm convention are fixed before phases are compared.

Require $Q^+=\mathscr D^*\mathscr D$ and $Q^-=\mathscr D\mathscr D^*$ to have the supplied nonnegative self-adjoint realizations with discrete spectrum, finite multiplicities and smooth eigensections, and the same positive spectrum with multiplicity. A spectral cut is a number $a>0$ not in either spectrum on an open parameter patch $U_a\subseteq T$. The orthogonal projections onto eigenvalues $\lambda<a$, including zero modes, must form smooth finite-rank bundles $V_a^\pm\subset\mathscr H^\pm$; their complements are denoted $\mathscr H^\pm_{>a}$. The finite cut line is $L_a=(\det V_a^+)^*\otimes\det V_a^-$. For $a<b$, the operator $\mathscr D$ is invertible between the eigenbundles $V_{(a,b)}^+$ and $V_{(a,b)}^-$. Glue $L_a$ to $L_b$ by tensoring with its top exterior power $\det\mathscr D_{(a,b)}$. Finite-dimensional cancellation of these invertible modes identifies each fiber with the displayed kernel/cokernel line, even where kernel dimensions jump. Tensor factors are kept in increasing cut order; parity is $\operatorname{ind}D^+\bmod2$ if graded lines are used.

For each cut, define the scalar function $\zeta_a(z)=\sum_{\lambda>a}\lambda^{-z}$ using the positive $Q^+$ eigenvalues with multiplicity and real $\log\lambda$. Admissibility requires convergence on an initial right half-plane, a specified meromorphic continuation to a connected domain reaching $z=0$, regularity there, and smooth parameter dependence of $\zeta'_a(0)$. The **Quillen squared norm** is $\|\ell\|_Q^2=\exp(-\zeta'_a(0))\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$. Finite bands satisfy $\zeta_a-\zeta_b=\sum_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda^{-z}$ and $\|\ell_b\|_{L^2}^2=(\prod_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda)\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$, which give cut independence of this norm. No existence of that continuation for an arbitrary Fredholm family is inferred.

Project $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ to the cut subbundles and their complements. They induce a connection $\nabla^a$ on $L_a$. On the invertible complement let $\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a}=\widetilde\nabla^-_{>a}\mathscr D_{>a}-\mathscr D_{>a}\widetilde\nabla^+_{>a}$. For $t>0$ define the complex one-form $h_a(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathscr H^+_{>a}}(\mathscr D_{>a}^{-1}(\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a})e^{-tQ^+_{>a}})$; the trace is the absolutely convergent sum of diagonal matrix coefficients in an orthonormal eigenbasis, independent of choices within each eigenspace. Require this convergence and the smooth coefficient expansion $h_a(t)=\sum_{j=-d/2}^{-1}b_jt^j+b_0+b_{\log}\log t+o(1)$ as dimensionless $t\downarrow0$. The finite-part convention is $\operatorname{FP}h_a=b_0+\gamma_1b_{\log}$, where $\gamma_1=\int_0^\infty e^{-r}\log r\,dr=\Gamma'(1)$; the equality names the usual gamma-function derivative and fixes the log-term subtraction. The **Bismut–Freed connection** in this convention is the local formula $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}=\nabla^a+\operatorname{FP}h_a$, as in Dai–Freed (3.6)–(3.7).

Admissibility further requires that these forms are smooth, intertwine the specified cut transitions, and are compatible with the Quillen norm: $d\|s\|_Q^2=\langle\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s,s\rangle_Q+\langle s,\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s\rangle_Q$ for every local section $s$. Thus in a unit frame the connection form is purely imaginary. Gauge identifications must intertwine all cut data, preserve this norm and preserve the connection after the corresponding parameter pullback. These are explicit mathematical conditions on the supplied regularization. Cut gluing reduces on a finite band to the determinant derivative $(\det\mathscr D)^{-1}\nabla(\det\mathscr D)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathscr D^{-1}\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D)$ with the induced finite-dimensional connections; analytic existence, smooth heat expansions and naturality for all geometric families are not asserted here. In particular a Hermitian line alone does not supply this connection. Parallel transport means the solution of $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}_{\dot A_t}s(t)=0$ with a specified initial value; in a unit frame with connection $i\beta$, it is multiplication by $\exp(-i\int\beta)$.

When the supplied real or pseudoreal fermion structure instead yields a skew-Fredholm quadratic form, include its actual **Pfaffian data**. Concretely, on a common dense Sobolev domain $W^1$ of a complex Hilbert space $W^0$, supply a bounded linear Fredholm map $B:W^1\to(W^0)^*$ such that $b(w,z)=(Bw)(z)$ is complex bilinear and skew on $W^1\times W^1$, with $\operatorname{coker}B\cong(\ker B)^*$ induced by the pairing. Supply finite spectral subspaces $W_a$ of $B^*B$ containing the kernel, with orthogonal cut bands on which $b$ is nondegenerate and no cross terms between bands. For a finite $2m$-dimensional space $W$ the Pfaffian is $\operatorname{pf}(b)=b^{\wedge m}/m!\in\det W^*$, interpreting $b\in\bigwedge^2W^*$; it is zero in odd dimension. Glue $P_a=\det W_a^*$ by the nonzero Pfaffians of the even-dimensional invertible cut bands. The resulting graded line $P$ has parity $\dim\ker B\bmod2$ and the specified natural square identification $P^{\otimes2}\cong L_B$, where $L_B$ is the displayed determinant convention applied to $B$. Its squared Quillen norm has high-mode factor $\exp(-\zeta'_{B,a}(0)/2)$, with $\zeta_{B,a}$ defined from $B^*B$ exactly as above. Its unitary connection is the one whose tensor square, under that identification, is the supplied Bismut–Freed connection of $L_B$; locally its connection form is half that determinant form in square-compatible frames. Smooth gluing, the square identification, spectral continuations, metric compatibility and gauge naturality are required Pfaffian admissibility data, not an arbitrary choice of a square root or an existence assertion for every real/pseudoreal theory.

Let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the affine space of smooth connections on $P$, and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the group of smooth bundle automorphisms covering the identity on $M$. A gauge arrow $u:A\to A^u$ induces a unitary map $u_*:\mathcal L_A\to\mathcal L_{A^u}$ by its action on kernel and cokernel. A closed loop in background/gauge-field space consists of a smooth path $A_t$ in $\mathcal A(P)$, $0\le t\le1$, and an endpoint gauge arrow $u:A_0\to A_1$. Let $\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ be parallel transport and $u_*:\mathcal L_{A_0}\to\mathcal L_{A_1}$ the endpoint gauge map. The closed-loop automorphism is $u_*^{-1}\circ\mathrm{PT}_{A_t}$ on $\mathcal L_{A_0}$. Its scalar is the holonomy $\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L)\in U(1)$. Fix the regularization and local-counterterm convention before comparing this loop phase with the infinitesimal local anomaly; the holonomy itself is additional global loop data.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an integer $d\geq1$, a compact smooth oriented Euclidean $d$-manifold $M$ with no boundary, its tangential structure (including a spin structure when the fields require one), and the model's boundary conditions. Let $\Gamma=(X,E_\Gamma)$ be the chosen finite regulator graph, with finite vertex set $X$. Fix a compact internal symmetry group $G$ with its actual global form and its action on every retained and integrated field multiplet. The symmetry is global, not a dynamical gauge redundancy. A **background groupoid** $\mathscr B$ is a category in which every arrow is invertible; its objects are the admitted nondynamical $G$-background data and its arrows are exactly the permitted background gauge transformations, including large transformations when the model admits them. The background data, local parameter charts on its object space, groupoid objects and arrows are part of the model input.

At each positive Wilsonian scale $\mu$ in a fixed interval $0<\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}<\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$, specify a finite-dimensional field configuration space $\Phi_\mu$ as a standard Borel space equipped with a model-chosen Polish topology $\tau_\mu$ that generates its standard Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and with a positive normalized Borel probability measure $\nu_\mu$ on $\Phi_\mu$. Its finite retained coordinate set is denoted $L_\mu$; on each sector component the continuous field coordinates are $\mathbb R^{L_\mu}$ with their Euclidean topology, and any topology and measurable structure on admitted sector labels are part of the model data. The chosen topology $\tau_\mu$ is used whenever a low-field open set or continuity in low fields is specified. For every background object $b\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathscr B)$, the dimensionless action is a map $S_\mu(-;b):\Phi_\mu\to\mathbb C$ that is Borel measurable, and $e^{-S_\mu(-;b)}\in L^1(\Phi_\mu,\nu_\mu)$. On each stated smooth local parameter chart of backgrounds, require $b\mapsto Z_\mu[b]$ below to be continuous in the chart topology. Define the finite partition functional by

$$
Z_\mu[b]=\int_{\Phi_\mu}e^{-S_\mu(\phi;b)}\,d\nu_\mu(\phi)\in\mathbb C.
$$

Require $Z_\mu[b]\ne0$ on every background patch where the effective functional is used. On each such patch choose a continuous branch $\operatorname{Log}_\mu$ and set $W_\mu[b]=-\operatorname{Log}_\mu Z_\mu[b]$; retain the transition phases when branches change on overlaps. If the action is real-valued, the integral is positive and this is the usual real-action case. For a complex action, the integral and logarithm are the explicitly specified complex-weight extension of the finite-regulator Wilsonian integral; the supplier definition for real Borel actions alone does not establish its integrability or nonvanishing. All field representations, regulator data, measures, normalizations, actions, scale-dependent coordinate splits and background boundary conditions are fixed model inputs.

More precisely, a **finite-regulator Wilsonian high/low integration** is specified at each step of a finite scale chain $\mu_0=\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}>\mu_1>\cdots>\mu_n=\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ (a single step is allowed). At step $j$, the retained coordinate set at scale $\mu_j$ is split as $L_{\mu_j}=L_{\mu_{j+1}}\sqcup H_j$. On each sector component, the associated Borel product identification is $\Phi_{\mu_j}\cong\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}\times\mathbb R^{H_j}$, and the scale measures factor as $\nu_{\mu_j}=\nu_{\mu_{j+1}}\otimes\nu_{H,j}$, where $\nu_{H,j}$ is a normalized Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^{H_j}$. Set the supplier's Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$ equal to $\mu_{j+1}$; the finite regulator, scale parameters, retained fields, integrated fields, and Borel ultraviolet action are precisely the data supplied to the finite-regulator model and Wilsonian-action definitions. In particular, when the optional Gaussian submodel is selected, its $M>0$, $E\geq0$, $\Lambda>0$, $A$, and $J$ satisfy the supplier's stated spectral, range, and cutoff conditions. For each retained configuration $\ell\in\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}$ and background $b$, require $h\mapsto e^{-S_{\mu_j}(\ell,h;b)}$ to be absolutely integrable with respect to $\nu_{H,j}$. On every open patch in the product of the declared topology on $\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}$ and a background-chart topology where the high integral is used, require it to vary continuously and remain nonzero, and choose a continuous logarithm branch. Then the complex Wilsonian action is the locally branched function

$$
S_{\mu_{j+1}}(\ell;b)=-\operatorname{Log}\!\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{H_j}}e^{-S_{\mu_j}(\ell,h;b)}\,d\nu_{H,j}(h)\right)-c_j[b],
$$

where $c_j[b]$ is the declared dimensionless local background counterterm assigned to that step (zero is allowed). For real actions and $c_j=0$, this is exactly the high-coordinate integral in the supplied Wilsonian-action definition. For complex actions it is the stated extension, with the absolute-integrability, continuity, and nonzero-branch conditions above. Scale measures are compatible products of the low-coordinate measures and these high-coordinate measures, so the full partition at each scale is the corresponding iterated finite integral. Every retained field and every retained topological sector is included at $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$.

With these product measures, the displayed action gives $Z_{\mu_{j+1}}[b]=e^{c_j[b]}Z_{\mu_j}[b]$ on the selected common branch and hence $W_{\mu_j}[b]-W_{\mu_{j+1}}[b]=c_j[b]$. Choose the logarithm branches compatibly along the chain; any transitions between local background patches retain their transition phases.

For each background-groupoid arrow, the model supplies the Borel identifications of the field spaces and the induced pullbacks on local partition branches. Each high-coordinate integration must intertwine those pullbacks, including their branch-transition phases; this is equivariance of the integration map and does not assert that each local scalar partition branch is gauge invariant. An **exact background-coupled RG comparison** is such a finite sequence of integrations for which the sum $C[b]=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j[b]$ is a single-valued admissible dimensionless local background functional and

$$
W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[b]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[b]=C[b]
$$

on each common local branch and compatibly on overlaps. Here local means an integral or finite-regulator sum of densities depending on background data and finitely many derivatives or neighboring cochains; the allowed counterterm space is fixed as part of the model. This definition records a finite-regulator flow interface and its locality hypothesis. It does not assert that such a flow exists for an arbitrary continuum QFT or that any continuum limit exists.

derivations.claim: By the common branchwise local BRST-variation assignment in [A4], applying the same infinitesimal background variation to $W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}=C$ identifies the difference of the endpoint representatives with $s\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}+d_Hq_3$ in the BRST complex of [F1]. This is zero in $H^{1,4}_{\mathcal C,\mathcal N}(s\mid d_H)$ modulo the admissible counterterms, so the local anomaly classes agree. The scalar identity is used only together with the explicit Wick-rotation and local-density hypotheses [A2, A4].

Let an admitted loop be represented by a path of connections from $A_0$ to $A_1$ and the closing gauge arrow $v:A_1\to A_0$. Equivalently, the forward arrow of [F2] is $u=v^{-1}:A_0\to A_1$ and its inverse induced line map is $v_*=u_*^{-1}$. By [A3], parallel transport along the path and the endpoint gauge identification both intertwine with the determinant-line isomorphism from the ultraviolet to the infrared. The two loop endomorphisms are therefore conjugate by that line isomorphism. Because each line is one-dimensional, conjugation leaves its scalar unchanged, so the holonomies agree under [F2]. This proves the global part without inferring it from the local BRST class.

boundaries.evidence: If no loop is admitted, the global assertion is vacuous; the local BRST identity in step 1.1 still applies to every local patch in the Statement.
When C=0, step 1.1 gives equal local variations and step 2.1 gives equal loop holonomies.
For the identity arrow and constant loop, step 1.1 has zero endpoint difference and step 2.1 has unit endpoint transition.
For a trivial symmetry or vanishing anomaly, the same algebra in steps 1.1 and 2.1 still applies.
Step 1.1 uses the relation at both specified finite scales μUV and μIR; it invokes no limit outside those endpoints.
The infinitesimal transformation in step 1.1 and the loop in step 2.1 are arbitrary admitted choices, so the conclusions hold for each such choice.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Assume Countable Choice: every countable family of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Fix a finite-regulator model on a compact, closed, oriented Riemannian spin four-manifold $M$, with its actual boundary-condition data, fields and jets, regulator, measure, and admissible local counterterms at every scale. Let $G$ be a compact finite-dimensional real Lie group serving as the internal global symmetry with fixed global form, let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $G$-bundle with supplied smooth connection $A$, let $V_R$ be a finite-dimensional Hermitian complex vector space, and let $R:G\to U(V_R)$ be a smooth group homomorphism. The admitted background groupoid has these nondynamical connections as objects and the selected background gauge transformations as arrows; the symmetry is exact and unbroken along the flow and is not a dynamical gauge redundancy. Fix a smooth family of Fredholm chiral Dirac operators $D^+_{A,R}$ and its inverse determinant line with the Quillen metric and Bismut–Freed unitary connection, with precisely the spin/Clifford, associated-bundle, induced-connection, Sobolev-domain, and admissible spectral-cut/regularization conventions of the determinant-line definition. On each background patch, the finite-regulator partition functional at scale $\mu$ is the local scalar representative of a section of that line, and its transition functions and endpoint gauge actions are retained.

Also fix a Minkowski coordinate region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with its orientation, spin structure, boundary-term convention, fields and jet domains, and identify it with the Euclidean local-variation problem by a specified Wick-rotation map. Here that map means an isomorphism between the complexified local background finite-jet algebras on the two patches, mapping the admitted background fields and horizontal forms and intertwining the horizontal derivatives and BRST differentials while preserving the declared boundary-term convention. Use the Minkowski patch's background-only finite-jet BRST complex, with nilpotent differential $s$ and horizontal derivative $d_H$; its local anomaly class is the relative cohomology class of ghost-number-one horizontal four-form cocycles modulo $d_H$ and the declared four-dimensional background counterterms. Write $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for the background-only finite-jet local density whose integral on this patch is the counterterm $C$. Assume an exact symmetry-preserving Wilsonian comparison from $\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ retains all remaining low-energy and topological sectors and satisfies $W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[A]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[A]=C[A]$ on each common local branch, for one admissible, single-valued, dimensionless local counterterm.

For the local anomaly conclusion, impose the following additional compatibility hypothesis. In the same regularization and boundary-term convention at both endpoints, the infinitesimal BRST variation of each branch $W_\mu$ is local in finite jets and is represented by the corresponding $a_{\mu,4}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ used in the local-anomaly definition: $\delta_s W_\mu[A]=\int_U a_{\mu,4}$ modulo the fixed boundary term. The specified Wick-rotation map carries these Euclidean variations to that BRST complex and commutes with its differential. The representative assignment is linear on the common branches, and the local counterterm assignment is compatible with it, so replacing a branch by that branch plus $C[A]=\int_U\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}$ changes its representative by $s\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}+d_Hq_3$ with $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}\in\mathcal C$ and $q_3\in\mathcal N$, where the same declared counterterm and boundary spaces $\mathcal C,\mathcal N$ are used at both endpoints. This is model and regularization data; it is not inferred from the scalar partition equality alone.

For the determinant-line comparison, take $C$ in the unitary phase convention so $e^{-C[A]}\in U(1)$. Assume the line-valued comparison induces a unitary isomorphism of the endpoint determinant-line families which, in local frames, is multiplication by the phase $e^{-C[A]}$ and which preserves the specified unitary connections and endpoint gauge identifications. Then the ultraviolet and complete infrared four-dimensional local BRST anomaly classes agree modulo the declared local counterterms, and the determinant-line holonomies agree on every admitted loop of background connections modulo gauge transformations. This is a conditional matching constraint only; it determines no infrared spectrum or gap and asserts no continuum limit or empirical result.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an integer $d\geq1$, a compact smooth oriented Euclidean $d$-manifold $M$ with no boundary, its tangential structure (including a spin structure when the fields require one), and the model's boundary conditions. Let $\Gamma=(X,E_\Gamma)$ be the chosen finite regulator graph, with finite vertex set $X$. Fix a compact internal symmetry group $G$ with its actual global form and its action on every retained and integrated field multiplet. The symmetry is global, not a dynamical gauge redundancy. A **background groupoid** $\mathscr B$ is a category in which every arrow is invertible; its objects are the admitted nondynamical $G$-background data and its arrows are exactly the permitted background gauge transformations, including large transformations when the model admits them. The background data, local parameter charts on its object space, groupoid objects and arrows are part of the model input.

At each positive Wilsonian scale $\mu$ in a fixed interval $0<\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}<\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$, specify a finite-dimensional field configuration space $\Phi_\mu$ as a standard Borel space equipped with a model-chosen Polish topology $\tau_\mu$ that generates its standard Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and with a positive normalized Borel probability measure $\nu_\mu$ on $\Phi_\mu$. Its finite retained coordinate set is denoted $L_\mu$; on each sector component the continuous field coordinates are $\mathbb R^{L_\mu}$ with their Euclidean topology, and any topology and measurable structure on admitted sector labels are part of the model data. The chosen topology $\tau_\mu$ is used whenever a low-field open set or continuity in low fields is specified. For every background object $b\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathscr B)$, the dimensionless action is a map $S_\mu(-;b):\Phi_\mu\to\mathbb C$ that is Borel measurable, and $e^{-S_\mu(-;b)}\in L^1(\Phi_\mu,\nu_\mu)$. On each stated smooth local parameter chart of backgrounds, require $b\mapsto Z_\mu[b]$ below to be continuous in the chart topology. Define the finite partition functional by

$$
Z_\mu[b]=\int_{\Phi_\mu}e^{-S_\mu(\phi;b)}\,d\nu_\mu(\phi)\in\mathbb C.
$$

Require $Z_\mu[b]\ne0$ on every background patch where the effective functional is used. On each such patch choose a continuous branch $\operatorname{Log}_\mu$ and set $W_\mu[b]=-\operatorname{Log}_\mu Z_\mu[b]$; retain the transition phases when branches change on overlaps. If the action is real-valued, the integral is positive and this is the usual real-action case. For a complex action, the integral and logarithm are the explicitly specified complex-weight extension of the finite-regulator Wilsonian integral; the supplier definition for real Borel actions alone does not establish its integrability or nonvanishing. All field representations, regulator data, measures, normalizations, actions, scale-dependent coordinate splits and background boundary conditions are fixed model inputs.

More precisely, a **finite-regulator Wilsonian high/low integration** is specified at each step of a finite scale chain $\mu_0=\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}>\mu_1>\cdots>\mu_n=\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ (a single step is allowed). At step $j$, the retained coordinate set at scale $\mu_j$ is split as $L_{\mu_j}=L_{\mu_{j+1}}\sqcup H_j$. On each sector component, the associated Borel product identification is $\Phi_{\mu_j}\cong\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}\times\mathbb R^{H_j}$, and the scale measures factor as $\nu_{\mu_j}=\nu_{\mu_{j+1}}\otimes\nu_{H,j}$, where $\nu_{H,j}$ is a normalized Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^{H_j}$. Set the supplier's Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$ equal to $\mu_{j+1}$; the finite regulator, scale parameters, retained fields, integrated fields, and Borel ultraviolet action are precisely the data supplied to the finite-regulator model and Wilsonian-action definitions. In particular, when the optional Gaussian submodel is selected, its $M>0$, $E\geq0$, $\Lambda>0$, $A$, and $J$ satisfy the supplier's stated spectral, range, and cutoff conditions. For each retained configuration $\ell\in\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}$ and background $b$, require $h\mapsto e^{-S_{\mu_j}(\ell,h;b)}$ to be absolutely integrable with respect to $\nu_{H,j}$. On every open patch in the product of the declared topology on $\Phi_{\mu_{j+1}}$ and a background-chart topology where the high integral is used, require it to vary continuously and remain nonzero, and choose a continuous logarithm branch. Then the complex Wilsonian action is the locally branched function

$$
S_{\mu_{j+1}}(\ell;b)=-\operatorname{Log}\!\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{H_j}}e^{-S_{\mu_j}(\ell,h;b)}\,d\nu_{H,j}(h)\right)-c_j[b],
$$

where $c_j[b]$ is the declared dimensionless local background counterterm assigned to that step (zero is allowed). For real actions and $c_j=0$, this is exactly the high-coordinate integral in the supplied Wilsonian-action definition. For complex actions it is the stated extension, with the absolute-integrability, continuity, and nonzero-branch conditions above. Scale measures are compatible products of the low-coordinate measures and these high-coordinate measures, so the full partition at each scale is the corresponding iterated finite integral. Every retained field and every retained topological sector is included at $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$.

With these product measures, the displayed action gives $Z_{\mu_{j+1}}[b]=e^{c_j[b]}Z_{\mu_j}[b]$ on the selected common branch and hence $W_{\mu_j}[b]-W_{\mu_{j+1}}[b]=c_j[b]$. Choose the logarithm branches compatibly along the chain; any transitions between local background patches retain their transition phases.

For each background-groupoid arrow, the model supplies the Borel identifications of the field spaces and the induced pullbacks on local partition branches. Each high-coordinate integration must intertwine those pullbacks, including their branch-transition phases; this is equivariance of the integration map and does not assert that each local scalar partition branch is gauge invariant. An **exact background-coupled RG comparison** is such a finite sequence of integrations for which the sum $C[b]=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j[b]$ is a single-valued admissible dimensionless local background functional and

$$
W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[b]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[b]=C[b]
$$

on each common local branch and compatibly on overlaps. Here local means an integral or finite-regulator sum of densities depending on background data and finitely many derivatives or neighboring cochains; the allowed counterterm space is fixed as part of the model. This definition records a finite-regulator flow interface and its locality hypothesis. It does not assert that such a flow exists for an arbitrary continuum QFT or that any continuum limit exists.

derivations.claim: Since $F_3$ is unchanged by every allowed gauge transformation, expanding $C_k[A_1+d\lambda_1,A_2+d\lambda_2,A_3+d\lambda_3]-C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]$ gives $\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4}(d\lambda_1\wedge A_2\wedge F_3+A_1\wedge d\lambda_2\wedge F_3+d\lambda_1\wedge d\lambda_2\wedge F_3)$. The final term is exact because $d\lambda_1\wedge d\lambda_2\wedge F_3=d(\lambda_1d\lambda_2\wedge F_3)$, using $dF_3=0$, so its integral vanishes on closed $T^4$. Integration by parts in the first two terms gives $-\int_{T^4}\lambda_1F_2\wedge F_3+\int_{T^4}\lambda_2F_1\wedge F_3$, which is exactly the displayed variation.

By [F2], the same $C_k$ is the admissible local term at both endpoints. Under the common local BRST-variation assignment [A2], the RG relation identifies the difference of the evaluations of the endpoint anomaly representatives on the allowed gauge parameters with the gauge variation computed in step 1.1. The local-density compatibility assumption of the theorem lifts this equality to the BRST representative of the counterterm density $\mathcal C_k=\frac{ik}{2\pi}A_1\wedge A_2\wedge F_3$, modulo a $d_H$-exact term, so [F1] places the difference in zero class in the four-dimensional anomaly quotient. The representatives may differ, but their local perturbative anomaly classes agree.

derivations.claim: Choose $R>0$ with $R^3\ge4|j|/\lambda$. For $r\ge R$, $\lambda r^4-2|j|r\ge(\lambda/2)r^4$; on $0\le r<R$, the continuous function $(\lambda/2)r^4-\lambda r^4+2|j|r$ has a finite maximum $K$, so $\lambda r^4-2|j|r\ge(\lambda/2)r^4-K$ for every $r\ge0$. Since the kinetic and mass terms are nonnegative, $S_j[\phi]\ge a^4(\lambda/2)\sum_x|\phi_x|^4-a^4KN^4$. In polar coordinates, each one-site factor $\int_{\mathbb C}e^{-a^4(\lambda/2)|z|^4}\,d^2z=2\pi\int_0^\infty r e^{-a^4(\lambda/2)r^4}\,dr$ is finite; the finite product over $N^4$ sites proves convergence of the full Boltzmann integral. Under the global rotation, the source summand changes from $j(\phi_x+\overline{\phi_x})$ to $j(e^{i\alpha}\phi_x+e^{-i\alpha}\overline{\phi_x})$, whose derivative at $\alpha=0$ is $ij(\phi_x-\overline{\phi_x})$.

Choose the allowed configuration $\phi_x=ir$ at every site with real $r\neq0$. The derivative of the full source term is $-2a^4j r N^4\neq0$. Therefore the fixed-source action is not invariant under $U(1)$, so this model cannot be the endpoint of an exact $U(1)$-preserving flow as required by [F1]. No anomaly-matching conclusion follows for this explicitly broken model.

risk_review.notes: Checked both Verification steps and all action parameters: N>=2, a>0, m0>0, lambda>0 and fixed real j!=0. The uniform quartic lower bound yields a finite product of convergent radial integrals; the polynomial used to choose K attains its maximum at r=(abs(j)/lambda)^(1/3)<R. The source-free kinetic, mass and quartic terms are U(1)-invariant; the allowed constant phi=ir has variation -2 a^4 j r N^4!=0 for r!=0. The source is not transformed as a spurion. Thus the theorem exact-symmetry premise fails, without a claimed anomaly value or RG existence. N=1 and j=0 are outside this example.
